reasoning: FairTix is a ticketing marketplace combating scalping through a lottery-based 'Fair Queue' system. The automation landscape reveals three core business processes: 1) User onboarding with welcome emails explaining the anti-bot verification requirements, 2) Lottery winner notifications with 24-hour purchase windows and transparent pricing (no hidden fees, 20% resale cap), and 3) Customer support triage using AI to classify inquiries and auto-respond to FAQs. The workflows show varying maturity - support classification has 362 versions indicating heavy iteration, while lottery notifications have multiple duplicate versions suggesting testing/development phases. Error rates are concerning: lottery notifications fail 36.1% of the time (direct revenue impact), support classification fails 12% of the time, and even the error handler fails 15% of the time. The demo/training environment context (dlschoolautomations@gmail.com, hardcoded test data) suggests this might be a reference implementation or automation course material, not production. Missing processes include actual lottery selection, payment processing, ticket delivery, resale listing management, and verification workflows - all mentioned in emails but not automated.
